clue.text: Bewilder Truss about folios

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other, so the bundle wraps the folio letters

parts.note: to truss is to bind up, as hay is bound into a bale; a bale is a trussed bundle
F is the abbreviation for folio, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: A political puzzle: someone baffled by the former Prime Minister Liz Truss and her paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Truss' reads as the politician's name; it is a bundle of hay, BALE, which goes 'about' FF.
explanation.definitionFit: To baffle someone is to confuse or perplex them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Article on literary work that attracts negative types

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
an ode is a lyric poem, a literary work

explanation.surface: A magazine article about a book that draws in pessimists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negative types' are negatively charged ions, not gloomy people.
explanation.definitionFit: The positive electrode draws negatively charged ions (anions) towards it in electrolysis.

clue.text: Gathering for sickly Oscar's leaving

indicators.note: leaving means that letter departs from the words before it

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ill means sick or sickly

explanation.surface: A get-together held because poorly Oscar is departing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathering' looks like a meeting; it is a gathered strip of fabric. FOR ILL loses its O.
explanation.definitionFit: A frill is a strip of cloth gathered or pleated along one edge, used as decorative trim.

clue.text: Reflection of sound around large island results in slurring of words

indicators.note: around means the reversed sound wraps the other letters
a reflection is a mirror image, so the sound word is written backwards

parts.note: a noise is a sound

explanation.surface: Echoes bouncing round a big island make speech come out slurred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflection of' turns NOISE into ESION, which goes round LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Elision is omitting a sound or syllable when speaking, as in 'don't', so words run together.

clue.text: Perhaps Trump briefly drinks and exercises

parts.note: Trump is an example of a president, and the short form of president is PRES
to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls, so drinks gives SUPS

explanation.surface: A picture of a famous politician who has a drink and works out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks Trump as one example of a president; 'briefly' trims that title to its usual short form.
explanation.definitionFit: Press-ups are gym moves done face down, pushing the body up with the arms: physical workouts.

clue.text: Gasp at that woman being a cougar?

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath
her is the pronoun for that woman

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at a woman, wondering if she's a 'cougar', an older woman dating younger men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cougar' suggests the slang for an older woman; the question mark flags it as the big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a big cat, and in the Americas the name is used for the puma, also called the cougar.

clue.text: Flag up region giving away American land

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: to flag is to tire or grow weary

indicators.note: giving away means a letter is dropped from the region word

parts.note: an area is a region

explanation.surface: Raising a flag over a region surrendered by the Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TIRE to ERIT; AREA losing an A leaves REA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country in the Horn of Africa, a land on the Red Sea coast.

clue.text: Spooner's magical method to remove unwanted plants such as this?

definitions.text: Spooner's magical method to remove unwanted plants such as this?

indicators.note: Spooner's signals a swap of the opening sounds of two words, after Reverend Spooner

parts.note: to weed is to pull out unwanted plants
a spell is a magical incantation or method

explanation.surface: A spell for getting rid of garden weeds, aimed at a particular weed.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the starts of WEED SPELL gives SPEED WELL; and that plant is itself a garden weed one might want gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell (veronica) is a small blue-flowered plant often treated as a lawn weed.

clue.text: Surprising plot to accommodate high value sporting event

indicators.note: to accommodate means the first jumble houses the second inside it
surprising suggests something unexpected, so the letters of plot are rearranged
high in the sense of intoxicated signals the letters of value are scrambled

explanation.surface: An unexpected storyline built around something precious at an athletics meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks part of 'high value'; it means 'intoxicated', a signal to jumble VALUE into EVAUL, held in POLT from 'plot'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole vault is an athletics field event where competitors clear a high bar using a long pole.

clue.text: Lackey follows party in government

indicators.note: follows puts the servant word after the party word in the answer

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party or celebration
a minion is a servile follower, just like a lackey

explanation.surface: A political underling trails behind their party once it holds power.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion means sovereign rule or authority over a territory, the power to govern.

clue.text: Dreams of ladies' pants

indicators.note: pants in British slang means rubbish or badly done, so the letters of the next word are messed up

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about fantasies involving women's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like a noun for underwear; in British slang it means 'rubbish', the signal to jumble LADIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are perfect visions one aspires to, the things a person dreams of achieving.

clue.text: Supporter of optimistic coin tosser?

definitions.meaning: someone who hopes you do well and backs you
a hopeful person flinging a coin down into a wishing well

explanation.surface: A fan of someone who flips coins and hopes for luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the hyphenated word: a person making a wish at a well.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-wisher is a person who expresses goodwill and support for someone's success.

clue.text: Dirty Den's rapid descent

definitions.meaning: a grimy, disreputable bar or club; also the nickname of the EastEnders villain Den Watts

explanation.surface: The nosedive of Dirty Den, the notorious landlord of the British soap EastEnders.
explanation.walkthrough: Dirty Den was a famous character in EastEnders, a long-running British TV soap; here the phrase just means a seedy haunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A seedy, sleazy bar is called a dive, and a sudden plunge downwards is also a dive.

clue.text: Wife struck Frenchman over fake cream in coffee

parts.note: struck means hit

indicators.note: over in a down-the-page or turned-over sense signals the French name is written backwards

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A domestic drama: a wife hits a Frenchman in a row over imitation coffee creamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like 'about'; here it means the French name is turned backwards. The definition is the whole of 'fake cream in coffee'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee whitener is a powdered non-dairy substitute that people add instead of real milk or cream.

clue.text: Understand growth in suffering

parts.note: to hear can mean to understand, as in 'I hear you'
a tache is a moustache, facial hair growth

explanation.surface: Grasping the growth of someone's pain.
explanation.walkthrough: TACHE is informal British for a moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional anguish or grief, a form of suffering.

clue.text: Moroccan entering a ground

indicators.note: ground as in crushed or milled signals that these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from Morocco walks onto a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a pitch; it is the past tense of grind, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tangerine is a native of Tangier, the Moroccan port city.

clue.text: A place where people gather in line

parts.note: a venue is a site where an event is held and people assemble

explanation.surface: Describes a spot where people assemble while queueing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in line' looks like one phrase about queueing; 'in' is only a link and 'line' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a line of approach, as in an avenue of inquiry, or a tree-lined road.

clue.text: Pre-recorded John Kelly?

parts.note: john and can are both American slang words for a toilet
Ned Kelly was the famous Australian bushranger and outlaw

explanation.surface: Asks whether some celebrity named John Kelly was taped beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: The full name 'John Kelly' splits into two pieces: a toilet and the outlaw's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Canned laughter or music is recorded in advance and played back, not performed live.

clue.text: Hybrid rose rapidly suppresses insectivorous plant

indicators.note: suppresses means the phrase holds down, keeping something concealed inside its letters

explanation.surface: A cross-bred rose quickly overwhelms a bug-eating plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Drosera is the genus name of the sundews, plants that trap and digest insects.

clue.text: Upset, as return of Miliband extremely overdue

indicators.note: return means the politician's first name is read backwards

parts.note: Ed Miliband is a British Labour politician
so means very or extremely, as in 'so tired'
something late is overdue

explanation.surface: Someone is upset because the Labour politician Ed Miliband's comeback is very late.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband is a former leader of Britain's Labour Party; 'return of' turns ED into DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate describes being bleak and miserable, deeply distressed by grief or loneliness.

clue.text: Rebellious pervert receives fine for verse

indicators.note: receives means the pervert word takes in a new letter
for means that new letter stands in place of the old one

parts.note: a deviant is a person whose behaviour, especially sexual, departs from the norm
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: A defiant degenerate is fined for writing poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receives fine for verse': DEVIANT swaps its V for F.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiant means openly resisting authority, boldly disobedient.

clue.text: The discontented dons curse warm clothing

indicators.note: dons as in putting on clothing means the curse word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: to curse is to swear

indicators.note: discontented means the contents, the middle, of the word The are removed

explanation.surface: Unhappy university dons curse while wrapping up warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university lecturers; it is the verb 'puts on', so the curse wraps round 'The' after 'discontented' empties its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater is a knitted jumper, a garment worn for warmth.

clue.text: Worst year to catch infection

indicators.note: to catch means the phrase holds the answer inside it, caught across the word gap

explanation.surface: Bemoans the worst year to fall ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small bacterial infection of an eyelash gland, making a painful red lump.

clue.text: Unfortunately, some gaffes are this?

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the letters of the next two words are disordered

explanation.surface: A politician's blunders sadly stray from the agreed line.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: gaffes are typically statements that stray from the party line.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-message means saying something that departs from the official party line, as embarrassing slips do.

clue.text: Spread goodness, except Thursday

indicators.note: except means leaving out the following letters from the exclamation

parts.note: strewth is a British and Australian exclamation of surprise, like 'goodness!'

explanation.surface: Kindness spreads every day of the week apart from Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goodness' reads as virtue; it is the exclamation 'Goodness!', whose British equivalent is STREWTH, which drops TH.
explanation.definitionFit: To strew is to scatter things untidily over a surface, so to spread them about.

clue.text: Good weather for cereal crops

parts.note: rain is a kind of weather

explanation.surface: Wet weather that is good for growing cereals.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain is the collective term for harvested cereal plants such as wheat and barley.

clue.text: Lively part of Macbeth where apparitions are summoned, ending in massacre

parts.words: part of Macbeth where apparitions are summoned
parts.note: the witches conjure the apparitions in Act IV of Macbeth, written ACT IV

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of massacre

explanation.surface: A lively scene in Shakespeare's Macbeth that ends in slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The witches' cauldron scene with its apparitions is Act IV, scene 1; IV is Roman numeral four.
explanation.definitionFit: Active means full of energy and movement, a direct synonym of lively.

clue.text: A second test, with time advancing, of main communication channel?

indicators.note: advancing means the time letter moves forward to an earlier place in the word

parts.note: a retrial is a second trial or test of a case

explanation.surface: Sounds like a second exam on the main route of communication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advancing' moves the T of RETRIAL two places forward, giving RTERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An arterial road or route is a major through-route, like an artery carrying the main flow.

clue.text: Appropriate and right to keep team, except that Wan-Bissaka finally replaces Maguire at the back

indicators.note: to keep means the right abbreviation holds the team word inside it
replaces signals one letter swapped out for another in the team word

parts.note: a football or cricket team is an eleven

indicators.note: at the back picks the last letter of Maguire
finally picks the last letter of Wan-Bissaka

explanation.surface: A football selection call: keep the team, but Wan-Bissaka comes in for Maguire at the back of defence.
explanation.walkthrough: Wan-Bissaka and Maguire are Manchester United defenders; 'replaces' swaps the team word's last letter, and 'to keep' puts the result inside the right abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevant means pertinent or applicable to the matter, so suitable and fitting here.

clue.text: Old women into gang fighting

indicators.note: into means the old-women letters go inside the gang word

parts.note: a ring is a gang of criminals, as in a smuggling ring

explanation.surface: Elderly women get caught up in a gang brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: Rowing (rhymes with 'cow') is British for quarrelling noisily, not using oars.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a row is a loud quarrel, so rowing means arguing or squabbling.
